- inputs/schedule-H9.yaml (lines 7-19): cuts [[grantor, c2]] upon Grant(c1), then issues request: c2 with no further faults.
- inputs/failure-model-v2.md ("Connected", F2.1) & inputs/schedule-format.md (Rule L3): defines "connected" as both directed links up and specifies that C1.4's premise requires a majority of lease nodes, storage, and the requester to be mutually connected, without requiring the current grantor to be in that majority or connected to the requester ("how a request reaches a node that can grant, and how the grant comes back, is the artifact's business").
- model-regen/Lease.tla (lines 142-164, Reaches and Grant) & model-regen/README.md (Interpretation 3): Reaches(p, q) allows one-hop relay through any running lease node (f \in Lease \ {p, q} : up[f] /\ Up(p, f) /\ Up(f, q)), allowing traces/model-H9-witness.jsonl (line 5) to issue Grant(proc: n1, seq: 2, client: c2, token: 12) after [["c2","n1"],["n1","c2"]] is cut (line 3).
- impl-regen/README.md ("Architecture and derivation", Interpretation 4): uses etcd Raft with PreVote and CheckQuorum; clients retry every lease node, but "A grant is published only by its originating leader" and Grant records issuance at the grantor, with no follower forwarding/relay of client requests and grant replies.
- traces/impl-H9-seed1.jsonl (lines 1-4) & traces/impl-H9-seed1.result.json: n3 (grantor_term 2) grants c1, env cuts [["n3","c2"],["c2","n3"]], c2 emits Request(seq: 1), and no further Grant is ever issued (events: 4, ticks: 621, FAIL C1.4 with clique ["n1","n2","s","c2"] stable for 600 ticks).
R_H9.reasoning: After c1 is granted by the initial leader (n1 in the model, n3 in the implementation), Step 2 cuts only the bidirectional link between that grantor and c2. The remaining two lease nodes (n1, n2), storage (s), and requester c2 remain up with all pairwise directed links up for the rest of the run, satisfying C1.4's literal premise under failure-model-v2 ("Connected") and schedule-format Rule L3. In the TLA+ model, Reaches(p, q) includes a one-hop relay through any running lease node, so c2's request and the leader's grant traverse a connected follower and H9 passes. In the Go implementation, the leader n3 remains connected to followers n1 and n2, so Raft heartbeats and CheckQuorum keep n3 as leader in term 2 and prevent n1 or n2 from campaigning. Meanwhile, c2's direct requests to n3 are dropped on the cut c2->n3 link, and although c2 retries followers n1 and n2, followers cannot issue grants themselves and do not proxy/relay client requests and grant replies to and from n3, leaving c2 unanswered for 600 ticks.
R_H9.same_class_as_prior: Something else (neither D1 nor D4): client-leader isolation under F2.1 partial partition with missing follower request/reply relay. Unlike D1 (quorum loss with a lagging follower) or D4 (a deposed lower-term leader blocking elections), the current-term leader here has a healthy, up-to-date lease-node quorum and is not deposed, so Raft has no lease-cluster fault to heal; the stall occurs because the leader is unreachable directly from the client while followers neither relay client traffic nor take over leadership.
R_H9.stall_mechanism: Cutting the bidirectional link between the active Raft leader (n3) and requester c2 leaves n3 connected to both followers (n1, n2), so heartbeats and CheckQuorum succeed and no election replaces n3. Because c2's direct messages to n3 are dropped on the cut link and followers n1 and n2 neither relay client requests/grants through the lease cluster nor assume leadership, n3 never issues or delivers a grant to c2.
R_H9.what_would_settle_it: Inspecting impl-regen's Go source and internal message trace would overturn this verdict if it showed that followers n1 and n2 already proxy client requests to the leader and relay grant replies back to the client, and that the failure was instead caused by an implementation bug in link-fault injection (cutting links beyond [grantor, c2]) or in request-retry handling.
